summary: Calhoun County, AL tower on Chimney Peak; register dates it to 1935, but 1947-49 Anniston Star reports show it erected 1948-49; overlook gated and hours-limited since 2024.

facts.design: 100' International Derrick tower with metal 7'x7' cab (NHLR); a 1949 newspaper gives 99 ft 9 in for the steel tower

access.note: Gate installed; overlook open daily 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.; overnight access limited from Feb. 12, 2024 (Jacksonville State University). Sources do not say whether the cab is open to climbing.

events.note: Five acres donated on Chimney Peak; Anniston Star said a fire tower would be erected there
Dedicated September 7, 1949 at Germanic Springs north of Jacksonville; described as a steel tower 99 ft 9 in high, built after about a year of construction
Windows and fire-finding equipment removed after repeated vandalism; Forest Service said the tower was still in use
Registered January 15, 2009 as US 759, AL 6; nominated by Thomas Kaufmann
Gate installed; overnight access limited effective February 12, 2024

corrections.why: Anniston Star items reprinted on the Forest Lookouts site describe a tower planned in 1947, steel arriving in 1948 and dedication in September 1949, which does not fit a 1935 CCC build. Human review advised, since the register itself says 1935.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1935 and a CCC build in the 1930s; the 1947-49 newspaper items describe the tower as being planned and erected then. The story follows the newspapers for construction dates and flags the register's date.
The register says 100 ft and the 1949 newspaper says 99 ft 9 in; the difference is under a foot. The record uses 30.5 m from the register.

notes_for_editor: Direct conflict on build date: NHLR says 1935 (CCC, 1930s); the Anniston Star items reprinted by Forest Lookouts describe construction in 1947-49. The Star originals were not checked; we relied on the reprints. Current condition of the tower is not confirmed by any source read; the JSU notice concerns the overlook. Owner is unverified (one social-media post could not be read), so none is stated. No staffing or fire history found for this lookout.
